tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-verification.md <<'EOF'
# TLS certificate verification

TLS certificate verification is enabled in every build, development builds included, and this applies going forward. Development and testing use self-signed certificates, which are verified like any other certificate. The project also records that HTTPS is used everywhere with no plaintext exception, backed by proper certificate management.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-verification.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-verification.md`. Its one paragraph states that certificate verification is on in every build, development builds included, going forward. It adds that dev and testing use self-signed certificates that are verified like any other, and that HTTPS is used everywhere with no plaintext exception.

That comes from three current decisions (#31, #32 and #35). I left out the retired earlier decision (#29) and any option of turning verification off.

The first Bash attempt failed with a parser error, so I wrote the file with the Write tool instead.
